title: Lumbar spine paraspinal muscle and intervertebral disc height changes in astronauts
finding: Lean paraspinal muscle fraction fell from 86% to 72%. Post-flight disc heights were not appreciably different.
limitations: Track muscle quality separately from spinal dimensions. Camera estimates cannot measure either.

title: Change in Lumbar Muscle Size and Composition on MRI with Long-Duration Spaceflight
finding: Paraspinal cross-sectional area decreased by 9.0% on average, with substantial variation between individuals.
limitations: Compare each astronaut with their own baseline. Association with exercise does not establish a prescription.

title: Changes in Vertebral Bone Density and Paraspinal Muscle Morphology Following Spaceflight and 1 Year Readaptation on Earth
finding: Regional vertebral bone loss and changes in muscle morphology persisted into readaptation.
limitations: Use dated clinical imaging for bone and muscle tissue metrics; never infer bone density from video.

title: Field Assessment of Sensorimotor Function Following Long-Duration Spaceflight
finding: Early post-flight testing showed slower stabilization and poorer walking performance, with task-dependent recovery.
limitations: Keep pre-flight and post-flight balance assessments separate from in-flight movement.

title: Kinematic Sensors Evaluation for Spaceflight Exercise Data Collections
finding: NASA describes marker-based in-flight capture and evaluates camera and wearable approaches for exercise data.
limitations: Motivates multimodal capture. This prototype’s single-camera pose model is not validated for microgravity.

title: NASA-STD-3001, Volume 2 — Human Factors, Habitability, and Environmental Health
finding: NASA already defines human-system requirements for spaceflight, including physical capabilities and equipment accommodation.
limitations: Map research hypotheses to existing standards. Proposed adaptations require expert review and validation.
